R&N_ITB,100,6961,790,7751,"Backfill placed for embankments, non-supportive and unpaved areas shall be compacted to at least 75% relative density (ASTM D 4253 and ASTM D 4254) for free draining soils containing less than 15% by weight finer than 75 micron sieve non plastic material or 90% of the maximum density as determined by ASTM D 1557for soils containing more than 15% material passing the 75 micron sieve.

Backfill placed below all the supports, roads and paved areas shall be minimum compacted to 85% relative density (ASTM D 4253 and ASTM D 4254) for free draining soils containing less than 15% by weight finer than 75 micron sieve non plastic material or 95% of the maximum density as determined by ASTM D 1557 for soils containing more than 15% material passing the 75 micron sieve.

A cap layer shall be placed to provide wind erosion protection in all the outdoor exposed areas. The cap layer shall be a minimum of 150 mm thick. The contractor to use soil-cement asphalt paving or sprayed-on polymer-based erosion inhibitors on that capping layer. Gravel layer is acceptable, as long as no erosion possibility is there due to water and wind. Gravel layer thickness 100 mm can be considered. However, this is subject to the Geotechnical recommendation.

For the design purpose, Design Ground water level shall be considered as per Geotechnical information, however  seasonal  variation  of  groundwater  and  capillary  rise  of  groundwater  shall  be  taken  into  the consideration for design and construction work and shall be substantiated before the start of design and construction work.

No foundations shall be supported on backfilled soil. Only less important and lighter foundation can be rested on backfilled soil subject to detail engineering and Owner's approval fulfilling the settlement requirement.
A  geotextile  layer  shall  be  put  between  the  filling  layer  and  the  soil  after  removal  of  top  layer  if recommended by EPC Geotechnical study."
R&N_ITB,100,6681,550,7231,"Selected fill shall have the following properties:

The material shall be of such nature and character that it can be compacted to the specified densities. It shall be free of all materials subject to decay, decomposition or dissolution, and of cinders or other material that will corrode piping or other material.
The intention is to use selected fill below structures, below pipelines, backfill to structures, roads, parking areas and hard standings etc."

R&N_ITB,101,6854,667,7521,"If the surface soils is susceptible to wind and water erosion these shall be stabilized with Cement. The soil and cement should be well mixed, moisture conditioned to within 1 per cent of optimum moisture and compacted to at least 98% of the maximum dry density. The optimum moisture content and maximum dry density of the soil-cement mixture should be determined by the ASTM D-558 test method. Traffic, except as required to maintain the surface of the soil cement in a damp condition, should not be permitted for at least 24 hours after final compaction.

For slope protection against erosion from wind, stabilization of surface soil with Type V Portland Cement as per ASTM C 150 may be adopted. For slope protection against erosion from water, slowing down of surface water is needed. To accomplish this, erosion control blankets, fibre rolls may be used. Erosion control blankets are usually woven type from a chosen material, with lots of ridges and obstructions. These materials are either synthetic or natural. Fibber rolls are also made of similar material as used in erosion control blankets but are rolled into large diameter logs. Coir type logs/ Logs made of rice/wheat straw also may be used. These logs are nailed into the slope to slow down the surface water. Tensar type geo-grids also may be effective. The source/ availability of the appropriate material is essential in selection of the technique, and it shall be duly approved by the Owner's engineer.
Gravel layer is acceptable, as long as no erosion possibility is there due to water and wind. Gravel layer thickness 100 mm can be considered."

R&N_ITB,102,7100,879,7979,"The safe working capacity of the pile(s) shall be determined by calculation using recognized soil mechanic principles and equations. The Contractor shall carry out a programme of preliminary test piling at site to verify his designs prior to commencing the installation of permanent 'working' piles. The maximum load applied during the preliminary pile testing programme shall be 200% of pile working load. The settlement limit in this case shall follow relevant applicable International/local standards. Upon completion of testing preliminary piles shall be cut down and abandoned, such piles may not be incorporated into the permanent works construction.

For the structural design of the piles the recommendations in ACI 318M-08/318RM08: 'Metric Building Code Requirements for Structural Concrete and Commentary' and ACI 543R -00 Design, Manufacture and Installation of Concrete Piles and the requirements of this OTS shall be followed.

Permissible pile settlements at under load for compression, tension and lateral load tests shall not exceed settlement criteria imposed by plant manufacturers, local regulations or shall conform with the BS 8004, whichever is the most stringent. R&N_ITB,"103, 104",7046,793,7839,"The  Contractor  shall  be  responsible  for  the  design  of  all  water-tight  (i.e.  water  retaining  and  water excluding) concrete structures.
The Contractor shall adopt the following design philosophy for the design of watertight concrete:

- All  water retaining/water excluding structures and cable tunnels shall be designed and detailed in accordance with BS 8007 (BS 8102, Type B construction) to achieve a performance level as defined in BS8102  for  a  Grade 2  structure.  Additionally,  all  cable  tunnels  that  are  founded  below  a  level determined as High Ground Water Level plus 1.5 metres (HGWL + 1.5 m) shall be tanked. Where it is determined that tanking shall be required, it shall be applied as a minimum to the underside of the base and to the walls up to the HGWL + 1.5 m level or shall totally enclose the tunnel if the top of roof slab level is below HGWL + 1.5 m level.

- Where the design deems that building basements are necessary, whether above or below ground water level,  then  these  shall  be  tanked  to  achieve  a  performance  level  as  defined  in  BS 8102  for  Grade 2 structure. The tanking shall be applied to the basement structure and extend up the walls to ground level

R&N_ITB,104,7090,888,7978,"The Steam turbine buildings shall provide protection of the equipment, electrical enclosed installation and controls from the environmental conditions. The buildings shall be designed for noise attenuation and be of non-combustible construction. The buildings shall be dust proof type and ventilated so that the building internal Design Temperature should not be greater than 5°C above maximum ambient temperature. The entrances shall be sufficiently sized to provide access for the largest item to be located within respective Building.

The  building  shall  be  of  sufficient  size  to  facilitate  the  installation  operation  and  maintenance  of  all components and equipment housed therein.  Requisite lay-down areas shall be provided for O&M purpose. Entrances shall be suitably sized and located to facilitate maintenance requirements.
Proper handling arrangement shall be provided for the equipment for O&M period.
Sufficient  capacities  of  cranes  shall  be  erected  for  normal  maintenance  of  the  gas  turbine  auxiliaries, including lifting heavy parts such as the casing and rotor.

Suitable access to the turbine building shall be provided to allow access for single complete rotors. A rotor unstacking area shall be provided with a suitable foundation to enable unstacking of a single rotor in the upright position and all necessary equipment shall be provided to manoeuvre and support the rotor. The turbine laydown/maintenance area may also function as the rotor unstacking area

The separate turbine enclosures will be foreseen with easily removable panel(s) that can be lifted by the crane and can be put aside and foresee walkways with railings, sufficient lighting, around the roof and around the roof opening(s) that, with a connection in between the walkways.
The separate turbine enclosure shall be foreseen with removable  beams to connect hoists in strategic locations, such as above the combustion chambers.

The floor slab within the building, which incorporates pipe and cable trenches shall be constructed of reinforced concrete laid flat and with local dishing incorporated adjacent to floor gully inlets. Floor drains shall discharge via a piped drainage network into oily water separators. Trench covers shall be designed to accept the appropriate floor loading according to their location and shall be manually removable.

Emergency exits fitted with panic escape bars shall be provided to all areas of the turbine buildings and annexes and boiler enclosures. Steel doors and frames should comply with the fire rating requirements. These openings must be kept clear of all obstructions."

R&N_ITB,104,6737,646,7383,"The GT and ST foundations shall be a monolithic raft supported by piles  if required as per the Geotechnical report.  The  exhaust  stack  may  be  supported  by  a  separate  foundation  or  incorporated  within  the foundation if required by the Contractor.
The contractor shall ensure that the following points are included in the GT and ST foundation works:
- a. A minimum rebar content of 80 kg/m 3  of concrete shall be provided.

- b. The design of the GT and ST foundation shall satisfy, in addition to an appropriate internationally recognized design code on machine foundations, the following codes: ACI 351,  CP 2012 and DIN 4024. CP 2012  requires an  internal  reinforcement cage system which is essential for the foundation to act as a homogenous mass and provide a second line of defence to the machine anchoring system with the holding down bolts. DIN 4024 provides guidelines for carrying out dynamic analysis."
R&N_ITB,105,7119,598,7717,"- c. The GT and ST foundation shall be isolated from the rest of the works by floor joints.
- d. The ratio of mass of the foundation to mass of the GT and ST plant shall be at least 2.

- e. To reduce the risk of dynamic compaction the maximum load on any pile supporting a GT and ST foundation shall not exceed 60 per cent of its working capacity during the normal operating conditions and shall not exceed 90 per cent in extreme conditions. For a foundation supported by soil the same limits apply to the allowable bearing capacity of the soil.

- f. The design  of  the  GT  and  ST  foundations  shall  include  the  thermal  effects  on  the foundation and its ability to withstand the extreme differential temperatures likely to be experienced by the foundation, during the construction as well as throughout its design life. Protective measures during construction shall be part of the design.

- g. The section  of  the  GT  and  ST  foundation  below  ground  shall  be  protected  with  a coating system to resist attack from the sulphate content in the soils and chlorides from the ground water. Further protection against corrosion of the reinforcement (which leads to expansion of the concrete and cracking) due to the severe chloride ion content of the soils and groundwater shall be provided as covered by the concrete section of this Specification.
- h. The GT and ST foundation shall be poured in one operation and construction joints are not permitted unless in exceptional circumstances and with the approval of the Owner/Owner's Engineer.

- i. The design, detailing and construction of the GT and ST foundations shall allow fully for  the  'buildability'  of  the  foundations,  particularly  where  congested  areas  of reinforcement are required.

- j. In addition to the static structural design the contractor shall prove the design of the turbine  supporting  structure  dynamically  by  modelling  the  bearing  points,  the foundation and the soil body together, taking the full consideration of the coupling effect and interaction between the three systems.

- k. The  design  of  turbine  supporting  structures,  if  applicable,  shall  be  same  as  that supporting the gas turbines except in some designs a table top structure and columns are erected over a mat foundation. The supporting structure if cast monolithically shall  be  analysed  with  due  consideration  of  the  flexibility  of  each  structural component.  If the table top structure is supported by springs the substructure may be  designed  as  a  static  structure  if  its  superstructure  proves  a  sufficient  isolation achieved by the springs.
The Contractor shall submit thermal curing procedures for the steam turbine and gas turbine foundations to the Owner/Owner's Engineer for approval prior to commencing construction of these works."

R&N_ITB,109,7056,944,8000,"All buildings in the Plant shall be paved with minimum 150 mm concrete extending from the edge of the building  for  a  distance  of  1.2m  with  proper  slope  to  drainage  Surface  Water  Drainage  System  and additionally asphalted paving shall be extending from 1.2 m up to a distance of 5.0m with proper slope to drainage Surface Water Drainage System if the soil is erosion prone due to water and wind.

A surface water drainage system shall be provided for the Plant. The design shall allow for the separate collection, treatment and disposal of surface water over the whole of the Site (arising from run-off of natural water from buildings, roads, ground surface, paved areas, etc.). All buildings shall be provided with roof drainage for disposal of surface water, and be connected to the surface water drainage system. The surface water drainage system shall be arranged and designed to effectively manage all run-off and discharge arising from the Site.
The Storm  water  Drainage  system  shall  be  designed  considering  100  years  rainfall  return  period  and rainfall intensity equal to the retention period.

Basements, cable and pipe trenches and tunnels shall be constructed with adequate provision for drainage. Floors to basements, trenches and tunnels shall be laid to falls and/or drainage channels provided therein. Any water entering the basements trenches or tunnels shall be routed to sumps and connected to the surface water drainage system. Where connection to the surface water drainage system is not practical, then provision to pump-out water from the trench or tunnel drainage sump, by permanent and/or portable sump pumps shall be made. Fire deluge water shall be gathered into storm water catch pits and discharged via main storm water system and prevented from entering tunnels.
Primary site drainage and sub-soil drainage shall be provided, where necessary, on external areas generally to protect the site from run off into building areas etc.

Storm water drainage sumps, pumps and electrical equipment shall be located to avoid hazardous areas. If unavoidable then the pumps and electrical equipment shall conform to the requirements in accordance with API and NFPA for operation in hazardous environments. Pumps shall be able to be withdrawn from the sump at surface level for maintenance and repair. The sump and valve chamber shall be equipped with access covers and ladders for maintenance purposes. The sump chamber shall be designed hydraulically so as not to impair pump performance.
Additionally,  ESIA  requirement  shall  be  completely  followed  for  storm  water  design  including  for  the requirement of Storm water basin."

R&N_ITB,"109, 110",6875,894,7769,"The  Contractor  shall  be  responsible  for  design  of  wastewater  drainage  system  complying  with  the Environmental Regulations and other applicable regulations with respect to wastewater. The Contractor shall provide the following to comply with local environmental protection requirements.

The Plant shall be designed with Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) which means that no emissions of liquid effluents  other  than  uncontaminated  storm  water  will  be  discharged  to  the  environment.  Hence,  all wastewaters will be directed to an evaporation pond  where the accumulating sludge will regularly be disposed.
The Contractor shall present a concept for the wastewater treatment plants and demonstrate the major waste water treatment steps including the corresponding maximum and normal flows.

Treated waste waters from operations that are known to produce effluents will be directed to a dedicated sump  where  they  can  be  neutralised  before  being  pumped  to  an  evaporation  pond.  Transformer compounds: provide storage contamination and separation facilities for oil spillage

- Main building plant drainage: oil spillage, effluent from HRSG cleaning, HRSG blowdown, air heater wash  and  other  non-oily  contaminated  sources,  provide  oil  separators,  chemical  treatment  and sedimentation facilities/evaporation pond.
The treated effluent shall be discharged by pumping or gravity, ultimately to the final discharge point.

Effluent discharged from station processes shall be treated to comply with local environmental protection requirements. Effluent discharged from station processes into the chemical drains, dirty drains and clean drains shall be routed directly, after treatment, to the final discharge point."

R&N_ITB,110,6808,585,7393,"A sanitary wastewater and sewage drainage system shall be provided to allow for the separate collection, treatment and disposal of foul water (arising from toilets, urinals, sinks, etc.).

The sanitary wastewater and sewage drainage system shall be laid in straight lines between manholes. The systems  shall  be  self-cleansing  and  function  with  the  minimum  of  maintenance,  and  access  shall  be provided so that it is possible to rod the whole of the drainage system. The effluent shall be directed to a self-contained package type sewage treatment plant. The quality of all temporary and permanent drainage discharges from the Site shall comply with the local authority requirements.
Sanitary  wastewater  shall,  to  the  extent  possible,  be  plant  internally  re-used  after  its  treatment  for irrigation purposes. Its sludge shall be used, if applicable, as fertilizer.

For this reuse, the PME's/NCEC's General Environmental Regulations and Rules for Implementation apply. The sewage system shall consist of a piping system with inspection manholes every  60 m and at each change of direction
The piping  and  collection  system  shall  provide  holding  capacity  adequate  for  a  72  hour  failure  of  the treatment system without overflow."

- Internal concrete.

The minimum lateral distance between adjacent individual spread footings bearing at the same grade on soil shall be B/2, where B is the footing width or diameter of the larger footing. For Square or rectangular footings, of width B, the minimum lateral separation distance should be no less than B.  Where the lateral spacing  is  less  than  recommended,  the  stress  distribution  between  the  adjacent  footings  should  be analysed.

Net design bearing capacities and settlement estimates for tanks shall be based on the assumption that the foundation soils underlying the tank are not significantly affected by adjacent tanks. The lateral distance between adjacent tanks should be limited to a distance B, where B is the diameter of the smaller of two adjacent tanks. If the tanks are spaced at a distance less than B, the differential settlement between the centre and edge could be about 15 percent larger.

R&N_ITB,91,6769,1004,7773,"- No single main equipment (GTU, STU, GSUT and HRSG) failure shall result in a Forced Outage of the entire Plant.

- No single auxiliary equipment (all other equipment than main equipment as specified above) failure shall result in the Forced Derating of Plant. The compliance with the above criterion requires to a large extent  redundancy  of  the  entire  auxiliary  equipment.  Following  examples  shall  illustrate  this requirement:
- The Plant shall have a redundant power supply concept for the auxiliary services (redundant UATs, MV - distributions, LV- distributions, DC-system, UPS- system)
- Electronic devices of the protection systems must be redundant in case process redundancy is not available, while the requirement doesn't apply to MV&LV protection relay.

- Redundant active equipment shall be powered from separate buses and physically segregated where feasible. The system design shall be such that the standby equipment shall be activated automatically when the control system detects a failure of the running equipment to perform its intended function.
- GT MCC shall have the redundant / double incoming CB, and divided to two buses, normal bus and essential bus bar, with bus-coupler."

R&N_ITB,92,6868,1242,8110,"- The capacity of MV, LV bus sections and the sources feeding the bus sections should be adequate to take the load of the other bus section when the bus coupler closes in case of supply failure to other bus section.
- The n-1 redundancy criteria shall be maintained for each switchboard/MCC.
- Redundancy shall be provided for cooling fans such that with one group of fan or oil pump out of service the transformer would deliver the rated output within the specified temperature rise.
- Battery and battery chargers shall be provided with N+ 1 redundancy. DC System contains 2 x 100 % Battery and 2 x 100 % Battery Chargers to meet the redundancy requirements.
- UPS shall be provided with N+ 1 redundancy.
- Each LV system switchboard shall consist of two bus sections with two incomers and one bus- coupler. Each incomer shall be supplied by 1x100% capacity transformer.

- Diesel Generator shall be provided with N+1 criteria, where EDG cum BSDG concept to be adopted. The DG sizing shall consider all possible scenarios, including emergency shutdown during black start operation. Emergency cum BSDG DG sets shall have the capability of testing even if respective block is in normal operation OR when the respective block switchgear bus have no voltage. 1 x 100% battery starting system will be applied for BSEDG.
- All electrical system switchboards shall be labelled for Hazard Risk category (HRC) as per results of ARC Flash assessment study using NFPA 70 or relevant IEC standards (as applicable).
- For Gas turbine package, redundancy concept of LV & DC distribution for equipment supplied by OEM would be of OEM's standard design."
R&N_ITB,92,6842,1059,7901,"Redundancy for control & instrumentation shall be as given below:

- All redundant instrumentation shall have the hot swap capability. Critical Redundant equipment shall be change over automatically in case of failure one equipment / Instrument. (For Gas turbine package, the hot swap capability is not applicable due to safety reason. Especially, it is not allowed to enter GT enclosure during operation, hence any person cannot access the instruments in GT enclosure.)

- In general, devices shall be preferred that contain intrinsic safety, to avoid expensive supervision/monitoring installations, possibly subject to failure (In Gas turbine package, explosionproof type instruments will be used in the hazardous area.)
- Where redundant equipment is installed, it shall be possible to perform maintenance and repair works on one equipment while the others are in service.

R&N_ITB,93,6962,942,7904,"- All protection signals leading to a trip of the Plant or to a load reduction shall use 2 out of 3 voting logic. For Generator Protection System, signal shall be achieved through 1 out of 2 with two multifunction protective relays shall be provided for generator.

R&N_ITB,101,6854,565,7419,"If the surface soils is susceptible to wind and water erosion these shall be stabilized with Cement. The soil and cement should be well mixed, moisture conditioned to within 1 per cent of optimum moisture and compacted to at least 98% of the maximum dry density. The optimum moisture content and maximum dry density of the soil-cement mixture should be determined by the ASTM D-558 test method. Traffic, except as required to maintain the surface of the soil cement in a damp condition, should not be permitted for at least 24 hours after final compaction.

For slope protection against erosion from wind, stabilization of surface soil with Type V Portland Cement as per ASTM C 150 may be adopted. For slope protection against erosion from water, slowing down of surface water is needed. To accomplish this, erosion control blankets, fibre rolls may be used. Erosion control blankets are usually woven type from a chosen material, with lots of ridges and obstructions. These materials are either synthetic or natural. Fibber rolls are also made of similar material as used in erosion control blankets but are rolled into large diameter logs. Coir type logs/ Logs made of rice/wheat straw also may be used. These logs are nailed into the slope to slow down the surface water. Tensar type geo-grids also may be effective. The source/ availability of the appropriate material is essential in selection of the technique, and it shall be duly approved by the Owner's engineer.
Gravel layer is acceptable, as long as no erosion possibility is there due to water and wind. Gravel layer thickness 100 mm can be considered."

R&N_ITB,104,6737,605,7342,"The GT and ST foundations shall be a monolithic raft supported by piles  if required as per the Geotechnical report.  The  exhaust  stack  may  be  supported  by  a  separate  foundation  or  incorporated  within  the foundation if required by the Contractor.

R&N_ITB,109,7056,944,8000,"All buildings in the Plant shall be paved with minimum 150 mm concrete extending from the edge of the building  for  a  distance  of  1.2m  with  proper  slope  to  drainage  Surface  Water  Drainage  System  and additionally asphalted paving shall be extending from 1.2 m up to a distance of 5.0m with proper slope to drainage Surface Water Drainage System if the soil is erosion prone due to water and wind.

A surface water drainage system shall be provided for the Plant. The design shall allow for the separate collection, treatment and disposal of surface water over the whole of the Site (arising from run-off of natural water from buildings, roads, ground surface, paved areas, etc.). All buildings shall be provided with roof drainage for disposal of surface water, and be connected to the surface water drainage system. The surface water drainage system shall be arranged and designed to effectively manage all run-off and discharge arising from the Site.
The Storm  water  Drainage  system  shall  be  designed  considering  100  years  rainfall  return  period  and rainfall intensity equal to the retention period.

Basements, cable and pipe trenches and tunnels shall be constructed with adequate provision for drainage. Floors to basements, trenches and tunnels shall be laid to falls and/or drainage channels provided therein. Any water entering the basements trenches or tunnels shall be routed to sumps and connected to the surface water drainage system. Where connection to the surface water drainage system is not practical, then provision to pump-out water from the trench or tunnel drainage sump, by permanent and/or portable sump pumps shall be made. Fire deluge water shall be gathered into storm water catch pits and discharged via main storm water system and prevented from entering tunnels.

Storm water drainage sumps, pumps and electrical equipment shall be located to avoid hazardous areas. If unavoidable then the pumps and electrical equipment shall conform to the requirements in accordance with API and NFPA for operation in hazardous environments. Pumps shall be able to be withdrawn from the sump at surface level for maintenance and repair. The sump and valve chamber shall be equipped with access covers and ladders for maintenance purposes. R&N_ITB,"109, 110",6875,1126,8001,"The  Contractor  shall  be  responsible  for  design  of  wastewater  drainage  system  complying  with  the Environmental Regulations and other applicable regulations with respect to wastewater. Net design bearing capacities and settlement estimates for tanks shall be based on the assumption that the foundation soils underlying the tank are not significantly affected by adjacent tanks. The lateral distance between adjacent tanks should be limited to a distance B, where B is the diameter of the smaller of two adjacent tanks.
